checks.label: Primary energy supply
checks.note: DUKES 1.1 total supply plus marine bunkers, less non energy use, with nuclear counted as electricity generated rather than reactor heat (DUKES 5.6), as the model does. Includes ambient heat, which DUKES counts under bioenergy and waste.

checks.label: Final energy consumption
checks.note: DUKES 1.1 final consumption excluding non energy use.

checks.label: Final electricity consumption
checks.note: Electricity delivered to end users. The model excludes refinery electricity, which DUKES counts as energy industry use.

checks.label: Final gas consumption, including heat sold
checks.note: The baseline maps heat sold to gas heating, so heat sold is added to the observed gas.

checks.label: Final liquid fuel consumption
checks.note: Petroleum products excluding non energy use, plus transport biofuels, which the model supplies through the liquid fuel store.

checks.label: Final coal and manufactured fuel consumption
Final bioenergy, ambient and solar heat
checks.note: DUKES bioenergy and waste final consumption includes heat pump ambient heat and solar thermal. Transport biofuels are counted with liquid fuels.

checks.label: Domestic electricity
checks.note: DUKES counts electric vehicle charging under road transport, as does the model.
checks.issue: One heating system mix is shared by all sectors, so domestic heating electricity follows the all sector heat pump and direct electric shares (open-items.md, Model).

checks.label: Domestic gas, including heat sold
checks.issue: One heating system mix is shared by all sectors. Homes use more gas and less oil and electricity for heat than services, so the model moves gas from homes to services (open-items.md, Model).

checks.label: Services final consumption
checks.note: Public administration, commercial, agriculture and miscellaneous.

checks.label: Services gas, including heat sold
checks.issue: See domestic gas: the shared heating mix moves gas from homes to services.

checks.label: Industry final consumption
checks.note: DUKES 1.1 industry including unclassified. The baseline is built from ECUK, whose industry total (227 TWh) is higher than DUKES because of boundary differences.

checks.label: Transport final consumption
checks.note: Including international aviation, as in DUKES. Fuel use for each mode is calibrated.

checks.label: Natural gas total demand
checks.note: Including gas for power, energy industry use and losses.

checks.label: Oil total demand
checks.note: Primary oils plus net petroleum products and marine bunkers, excluding non energy use. Biofuels are excluded on both sides.

checks.label: Coal, manufactured fuel and other thermal fuel demand
checks.note: The model's coal backup share also covers other thermal generation, mainly waste, so DUKES 5.6 other thermal fuel is added to the observed coal. Blast furnace and coke oven fuel is included on both sides.

checks.label: Bioenergy, ambient and solar heat total demand
checks.note: Other thermal fuel (waste) is moved to the coal check, matching the model.

checks.label: UK electricity generation
checks.note: All generating companies, including storage output. Modelled generation is total supply less imports.
checks.issue: Storage output is low, see the storage check.

checks.label: Gas generation
checks.note: Shares of dispatchable generation are inputs. The total comes from the hourly balance.

checks.label: Electricity storage output
checks.issue: The optimal dispatch shaves backup peaks but does not arbitrage against prices, so storage cycles less than real storage (open-items.md, Model).

checks.label: Peak electricity demand
checks.note: End use demand grossed up for losses, highest hour in the ten weather years, against the 2024 simultaneous maximum load met. The model peak includes demand met by embedded generation and the coldest of ten winters, so it is expected to be higher.
checks.issue: The model peak is higher than any year in DUKES 5.10 since 2010 (open-items.md, Model).

checks.label: Dispatchable capacity
checks.note: The model sizes backup to the highest hourly need, with no reserve margin or outages, so it should be lower than installed capacity.
checks.issue: Backup capacity, and its cost, is a third below the installed fleet, which also covers outages and a reserve margin (open-items.md, Model).
